assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural demand estimation with endogenous prices, together with dynamic oligopoly and entry models, changed empirical industrial organisation. It is now the standard toolkit in merger review, antitrust and regulatory analysis. The conceptual advance is large and the policy use is wide.
assessment.attribution: The BLP random-coefficients framework (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a clear, compact core. Pakes also has foundational work on dynamic games, patents and productivity. Bresnahan and Reiss are important in the wider field but fit a different strand. Benkard and Levin are significant but less central. A three-person set is natural.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the 1990s and has had decades of validation and diffusion. The field has not been recognised by a prize as a structural estimation tradition, so the timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would rather credit Bresnahan or Reiss for the entry and market-power strand.
Whether the contribution is read as method or as economic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, micro-founded price setting and the theory of rule-based monetary policy underpin modern central-bank practice. The impact on policy and on macroeconomic theory is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credit is crowded. Calvo is associated with staggered pricing, Taylor with the policy rule and staggered contracts, and Woodford with the integrated theory. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are also major, so any trio leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work is decades old, widely confirmed and institutionalised. Some of its policy lessons were tested by the post-2008 and post-2021 inflation episodes.
uncertainties: The appropriate trio is contestable and could instead feature Gali or Christiano and Eichenbaum.
The framework's performance during the 2021–23 inflation episode is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation research quantifies how the distribution of resources across firms accounts for cross-country income and TFP gaps. It links micro data to aggregate growth and development, and has generated a large empirical literature.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the central paper and the pair is a clear core. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) is closely related, and Restuccia is on this list but Rogerson is not credited here, which complicates a three-person set.
assessment.maturity: The agenda is about 15–20 years old and widely replicated and extended. Debate continues about measurement error and the interpretation of wedges, so evidence is substantial but not final.
uncertainties: Whether Rogerson's omission from the credited names weakens the attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki–Moore (1997) provides the foundational account of how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It shaped the post-2008 understanding of financial crises and macro-prudential policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist link it to the financial accelerator, and Bernanke's share of that strand was already recognised in 2022. Adding Gertler is possible but would dilute a clean pair.
assessment.maturity: The work is nearly three decades old and has been confirmed by the financial-crisis experience and by a large body of empirical and quantitative work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for banks and financial crises may count against the field.
Whether the committee would add Gertler.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped trade theory and empirics. They explain who trades and how aggregate gains arise, and they supplement the earlier recognition of new trade theory.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central paper. Helpman has a long record of building the framework, including the Helpman–Melitz–Yeaple work. Redding is a strong contributor to the quantitative extensions, but the set is clearer with two or three names.
assessment.maturity: The agenda is more than 20 years old and standard in graduate training. Its empirical predictions are broadly supported, with some debate about the size of the gains.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the Krugman 2008 prize on trade.
Credit for the heterogeneous-firm approach is shared with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labour demand, wage inequality and the distributional costs of trade. The policy and political relevance is high.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the trade-shock work. Hanson is central to the local labour-market effects of import competition. Dorn is a co-author of the trade-shock papers, and Katz has long-standing work on skill-biased technological change, so the credit is spread across several people.
assessment.maturity: The work spans about 20 years, with the China-shock papers from the 2010s. It has high impact and an active empirical debate. Long-run consequences and the AI-era relevance are still developing.
uncertainties: Debate over how large and persistent the China-shock effects are.
The task framework's origins also run through Acemoglu, who has already been recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built the modern political economics of electoral rules, constitutions and fiscal outcomes, with unified theory and empirical tests. The field is broad and influential, and it follows the recognition of institutions in 2024.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clear joint authors of the core books and papers. Besley is a major contributor on state capacity and accountability and could be added, but the dominant credit lies with the pair.
assessment.maturity: The agenda is more than 25 years old and has been extended empirically by many others. Causal identification of constitutional effects remains difficult.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize for institutions and prosperity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical optimal-tax tradition links behavioural elasticities such as taxable income to optimal policy design using sufficient-statistics methods. It has had considerable influence on tax research and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod and Saez are the main figures in taxable-income elasticities, and Chetty in the sufficient-statistics approach. Stantcheva extends the work to dynamic and behavioural settings. Credit overlaps with the inequality and mobility candidates, and with Feldstein, who is deceased.
assessment.maturity: The elasticity-of-taxable-income work is about 30 years old. The newer strands are younger and still being tested. The empirical identification of the elasticity is contested.
uncertainties: Credibility of elasticity estimates and their sensitivity to specification.
Overlap in credit with the inequality and mobility candidates.
Whether younger contributors such as Chetty and Stantcheva are better recognised later.
